What type of wireless are you using? 802.11n/a/b/g? I see your router is a dual-band device. You should make sure any home device that will connect a 5GHz is using that band and only use the 2.4GHz band for devices that do not support 5GHz.

Something else to do would be to see what the wireless spectrum in your area is like. There are any number of apps you can use out there for this, but on the Android platform I think you get more details. I like Wifi Analyzer. It can tell you what channels are in use around you and let you pick one that is less crowded. You want to stick with 1, 6, or 11 in the 2.4GHz band. In the 5GHz band I usually just find one far away from the other stuff. Depends on how many other 5GHz wireless routers are around you.

Make sure your wireless router is central to your home and higher up than sitting on a desk or shelf behind some books. Keep the antennas at a 90 degree angle to the floor, too.

Wireless drivers on devices can also cause a lot of problems. Make sure they're updated.
